messages:
zara: Heads-up from today's onboarding run for atlas-32k int4. Observed an odd "stitch/handshake" anomaly when folding a large prefill + append sequence. Pattern: prefill ~12k tokens, append ~7k, resume. Intermittent small duplication (usually 3-6 tokens) near the join and then KV fingerprint flips. Repro rate low (~1/400) but reproducible with our tiny harness.

pip: Which env and policy? Any logs?

zara: Perf-lab node perf-19, kv_policy=fold (we need low latency). If we force kv_policy=reset it's clean but adds ~20ms P50 which is unacceptable for this workload. Short failure excerpt below.

```
[cache] prefill id=0x4c1d fp=0x5f2a len=11968 slot=13 epoch=101
[cache] append id=0x4c1e fp=0x5f2b len+=7168 slot=13 epoch=101
stitcher: phase_handshake: expected_seq=0x2b got_seq=0x2b
stitcher: posshift_mode=dynamic recompute
gen: step=11973 token=822 dup_range=11971-11976
[cache] fp_mismatch pre_fp=0x5f2a post_fp=0x5f2b
```

mike: Two hypotheses: 1) posshift recompute on append leads to RoPE discontinuity (phase drift) and duplicated tokens; 2) metadata/epoch write ordering race where append publishes new slot metadata before the generator snapshot completes, producing a mixed view.

flo: Did you capture per-layer phase checksums? That would tell if a layer's rotational phase changed across the stitch.

zara: Yes 10: added a light-weight per-layer checksum hook in the stitcher for this run. On the failing trace layer 18 and 23 show checksum deltas after stitch.

pip: Layer-specific diffs are telling. If only a subset of layers flips, could be a per-layer posscale clamp or a bad per-layer index calculation when applying appended slot offsets. Can you paste the layer checksums?

zara: Pasted minimal per-layer diff snippet: 

```
layer_checksum(before)[...]= [0x1a,0x2b,0x3c,...,0x9f]
layer_checksum(after)[...]=  [0x1a,0x2b,0x4c,...,0x9f]
changed_layers = [18,23]
```

mike: That narrows it. Two possible causes: indexing math in the stitcher (off-by-one for those layers) OR a race where append writes partial layer metadata while generator reads some layers. Which arch did you hit? Rerun on both x86 and arm64.

zara: We saw slightly higher frequency on arm64. I suspect weak ordering exacerbates it.

flo: For experiments: 1) run a 100k deterministic microbench (seeded RNG) in qemu-int4 with the phase-check hook enabled; 2) add a temporary epoch-handshake: append must perform CAS on the slot header and return an ack token; stitcher validates ack before applying dynamic posshift. If CAS eliminates repro, it's ordering. 3) alternatively force posshift_mode=continuity to skip recompute and see if dup disappears.

pip: Also add a quick micro-optimistic fix: when doing append->merge, publish a small epoch-token (u64) with membar semantics; generator reads epoch-token before reading slot payload. That gives low-overhead ordering without a full mutex. Worth trying as an A/B.

zara: Implemented both toggles in branch onboard/atlas32k/phase-handshake. Pushed unit test harness that loops prefill+append+resume for 100k iterations (qemu-int4) and records any per-layer checksum diffs + slot header snapshots to /artifacts/atlas32k/2812345678/.

ci-bot: Created issue #5599: "atlas-32k: stitcher phase-handshake vs posshift recompute causing intermittent duplication" (reporter: zara) :bug: (link: /artifacts/atlas32k/2812345678/)

mike: If the epoch-token CAS + membar removes repro, we can design a compact protocol: append writes slot payload, does atomic compare_exchange on slot.header.epoch to new_epoch, generator validates epoch before reading. No global locks.

flo: If forcing posshift_mode=continuity removes dup too, we have a second independent failure mode: posshift recompute edge-case. Might need a posshift-sanity check at stitch (e.g., compare per-layer expected phase delta to computed delta and reject recompute if delta > threshold).

pip: Also validate the quantized kernel path: sometimes quantized int4 kernels apply per-layer scaling in slightly different order which can amplify phase sensitivity. Ensure unit tests run with same kernel ordering as Dedicated.

zara: Will run the 100k suite across both archs and both toggles (CAS-on/CAS-off, continuity-on/continuity-off). If CAS removes repro while continuity toggle still fails occasionally, we'll land the epoch-token handshake as a hotfix and keep posshift sanity as follow-up.

mike: One more check: capture raw token ids around the duplication and run them through a tokenizer diff. Sometimes tokenizer boundary differences look like duplication but are actually merge/bytepiece misalignments. But your layer checksum finding points to RoPE/phase.

zara: Included token dumps and tokenizer diffs in the artifact bundle. Running the full 100k now; will update thread with results. TL;DR: intermittent duplication at prefill+append join for atlas-32k int4; added per-layer checksums, epoch-token CAS membar experiment, and posshift continuity toggle to triage race vs phase recompute.
